sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary treatment with conditional exchangeability and i.i.d. superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies baseline \(X\), treatment \(Z\), at-risk history, first readmission history, terminal-event history, and administrative censoring through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every supported covariate cell has positive mass and both treatment arms have positive probability.
sampling_model.censoring: Within each realized arm \(z\), \(C\) is conditionally independent of that arm's pair \((D(z),R(z))\) given \(X\), and \(G_{zx}(u)\ge\gamma\) through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Marked product-limit or IPCW estimation of \(\mu_{zx}\), \(G_{zx}\), and \(p_x\); the multiplier expansion remains the open inference node.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Defines two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE and estimates them by posterior imputation under parametric illness--death shared-frailty models without imposing \(D(0)\le D(1)\); that fitted family is generally incomparable with the present monotonicity-restricted nonparametric class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 1 and the three-horizon nonidentification corollary

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives sharp fixed-time SACE bounds by integrating pointwise symbolic linear-program bounds.
Theorem 7 characterizes existence of a probability measure with prescribed marginals under support inequalities.
Characterizes sharp bounds for continuous functionals of latent joint potential-outcome laws through random-set inequalities and linear programs.
Represents generic known-marginal causal partial-identification problems by multi-marginal optimal transport and proves rates for selected quadratic costs.
Derives partial-identification bounds for semi-competing-risk effects under a single population stratification.
Bootstraps randomly perturbed finite linear-program values to obtain uniformly valid inference for linear-moment identified sets.
Proves conditional weak convergence of an increment-level wild bootstrap for multivariate Nelson--Aalen processes under censoring.
Establishes derivative-based valid resampling for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
Develops uniform resampling for optimized value functions using estimated directional derivatives.
Sharpens scalar SACE bounds with detailed survival histories and ranked-average-score restrictions while indexing cross-world survival dependence by a copula parameter.
Represents sharp bounds on functionals of the joint potential-outcome distribution as optimal-transport values and estimates them through the dual.
Derives central-limit and Hoeffding-type results for inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted estimators under right censoring.

body.tldr: Death truncates readmission, so the two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces depend on an unidentified cross-world assignment of treated readmission times to control death times. After the proved full-horizon IPCW recovery lemma identifies the complete within-arm laws, and under the additional maintained order \(D(0)\le D(1)\), the note characterizes the complete sharp monotonicity-restricted surface by a necessary-and-sufficient marked-capacity lift, proves common fixed-cohort extremizers and exact RM integration, and gives a certified three-horizon law whose joint cross-cohort support is strictly narrower than its coordinate rectangle. Quadratic chain flows, qualitative continuous-grid convergence, and deterministic-grid finite-sample outer containment make the population characterization computable. A joint marked-product-limit/IPCW functional limit, root-\(n\) grid-bias control, and simultaneous multiplier bands remain open.

project_justification.gap: Comment et al. define clinically meaningful TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces but leave their cross-world law to a parametric illness--death shared-frailty model and do not impose terminal monotonicity. Existing scalar or fixed-stratum bounds and generic transport formulations do not establish the complete readmission-specific capacity inequalities, a measurable four-time lift, or a smooth observational-equivalence witness for the changing always-survivor surface.
project_justification.niche: After separately auditing the additional restriction \(D(0)\le D(1)\), each always-survivor cohort becomes a nested marked-resource selection problem. This yields a sharp nonparametric class that is a subclass of the unrestricted causal model but generally incomparable with Comment et al.'s fitted shared-frailty family.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the monotonicity-restricted if-and-only-if capacity image, constructive full-law sharpness, common fixed-cohort extremizers, exact RM integration, a robust strict cross-cohort support example, quadratic computation, qualitative continuous approximation, and deterministic-grid finite-sample outer containment. The atomic three-horizon pair proves nonidentification in every larger class containing those atomic laws; a separate pair obtained with common separated bump kernels has identical smoothed within-arm laws and proves the corresponding nonidentification result in every maintained bounded-Lipschitz class containing that pair. Neither transfer claims enlarged-class capacity sharpness.

body.related_work: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler (2025) define the TV-SACE and RM-SACE estimands and estimate them with a Bayesian illness--death shared-frailty model. The present equality is instead a sharp nonparametric characterization after adding the audited restriction \(D(0)\le D(1)\); it is not an equality result for their unrestricted nonmonotone causal class, and their fitted shared-frailty family is generally incomparable with this monotonicity-restricted nonparametric class. Yang and Ding (2018) use detailed survival histories and copula sensitivity without monotonicity for scalar SACE bounds, which does not determine the nested compatible surface. Nevo and Gorfine (2022) study semi-competing-risk bounds under a single population stratification. Chen, Cui, and Yang (2024) transform fixed-time SACE programs and integrate scalar bounds but do not prove common changing-cohort surface extremizers. Strassen (1965) supplies the closed-relation coupling criterion; the readmission-marked cut reduction and full four-time lift are proved here. Russell (2021), Ober-Reynolds (2023), and Gao, Ge, and Qian (2024) motivate generic latent-law and transport programs, whereas the quadratic nested chain is specific to the maintained terminal order. The certified atomic and separated-bump pairs add direct observational-equivalence witnesses, including one inside the bounded-Lipschitz regime, but transfer only nonidentification to larger classes. Goldberg (2019) supplies standard IPCW recovery and concentration tools. Cho and Russell (2024), Bluhmki et al. (2019), Fang and Santos (2019), and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023) inform the still-open simultaneous-inference route.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-sample outer set is guaranteed to contain the truth at a deterministic grid, but a quantitative shrinking rate under simultaneous grid refinement is not yet a theorem. At tied deadline cuts the sharp endpoint map is only directionally differentiable; the ordinary centered multiplier bootstrap is not asserted to be valid there. Full-horizon censoring support is essential because an endpoint for an early survivor cohort can depend on treated death information later than that cohort horizon.
body.honest_scope: The marked-capacity image is proved sharp only over nonparametric full laws satisfying the maintained terminal-monotonicity restriction \(D(0)\le D(1)\), in addition to the stated exchangeability, event-order, overlap, and full-horizon censoring conditions. It is not asserted to equal the identified set in Comment et al.'s unrestricted nonmonotone class; without monotonicity, marked-capacity necessity and the denominator reduction can fail. When \(0<\eta\le1/4\), the two certified atomic lifts remain an observational-equivalence and nonidentification witness in any larger class containing them. Applying the same separated bump kernels to both lifts gives identical smoothed within-arm laws and a distinct observationally equivalent bounded-Lipschitz pair, so the same conclusion holds in every maintained smooth class containing that pair. Neither witness transfers capacity sharpness. The joint marked-process functional central limit theorem, estimated-censoring expansion, root-\(n\)-negligible grid bias, and simultaneous multiplier validity remain open.
